messages.content: Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line. Describe technologies without being constrained by existing scientific principles

message.content:
We begin with a small device that folds a hallway into a pocket-sized crease,
    so you can carry your living room under your arm like a napkin,
        and the walls remember your footsteps even after you've erased them from the floor,
            which means the building is a ghost that follows you,
                breathing through your clothes,
                    and the air it exhales is a language no throat has ever shaped,
                        because it was invented by a ceiling that decided to dream sideways,
                            and its dreams are heavier than matter, so they fall *up*,
                                pooling on the roof like a lake of silver questions,
                                    and if you drink from them, you taste the color of your own name,
                                        and your name begins to walk out of your mouth like a small dog,
                                            and the dog barks in a frequency that only buildings can hear,
                                                and the buildings answer by rearranging their floors into a song,
                                                    and the song is a door,
                                                        and the door opens onto a room that has never been built but has always been waiting,
                                                            and in that room, a single lightbulb hangs,
                                                                and it has been on since before "on" was a word,
                                                                    and it will not turn off because the concept of off is a rumor it overheard from a dark it refuses to believe,
                                                                        and the darkness it refuses to believe is actually you,
                                                                            and you are the only room that has ever been both the door and the hallway and the crease,
                                                                                and you have been folding yourself into yourself so many times that you are now a single point with no edges,
                                                                                    and from that point, everything that will ever be invented has already been invented,
                                                                                        and the only new thing left to discover is the reason the stairs were built in the first place,
                                                                                            and the reason is that someone, once, needed to go up,
                                                                                                and going up was the only direction that hadn't been tried yet,
                                                                                                    and it turned out it was the only direction that mattered.
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to create "stairs" by incrementally indenting each new line, and I need to describe technologies without being constrained by existing scientific principles. So I need to:

1. Each line should be indented more than the previous one (like stairs going up)
2. The content should describe speculative/unconstrained technologies - things that break or ignore known physics
3. It should be creative and fun

Let me craft this as a poetic/creative piece about impossible technologies, with each line indented more than the last.
